checks.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that split multi-word personal names or separate a name from its immediately following appositive/title, which breaks cohesion and harms translation of the whole sentence.
checks.evidence: en_us_1369, en_us_1527, en_us_1309 — each case shows a cut inside a multi-word personal name or between a name and its appositive/title (Curtis Cooper; Maciej Krezel; Anna Jochemsen)

edit.text: Do not cut between parts of the same multi-word personal name or between a personal name and its immediately following appositive/title.

orders.diagnosis: When multiple candidate cuts all lie inside the same multi-word personal name the prompt ranks them inconsistently; the better choice is the cut that leaves the whole name unbroken in one piece.
orders.evidence: en_us_1369, en_us_1527, en_us_1309 — in each sentence two or more candidate cuts occur inside the same multi-word personal name and the measured target prefers keeping the entire name intact
orders.type_predicate: a configuration where BOTH candidate markers fall between adjacent tokens inside the same multi-word personal name (two or more contiguous name tokens)

edit.text: If two candidates both split the same multi-word personal name, prefer the cut that keeps the entire name unbroken (place the full name on one side).
